#### Why the gloom?

Page 5

• Doubts about the data, and a disconnect between economic reality of most Chinese people and investors

• Credit agencies are down-grading and investors are looking for the exit…”uninvestable”

• 2023 was lowest level of FDI since 1990s (Essity is the latest in our world, following Stora Enso in 2022). Q2 2024 FDI was -$14.8bn, worst on record.

• “De-coupling”, “de-risking”, “peak China”.

#### China Property sector “slow-motion train wreck”

Page 7

• Property sector accounts for up to 30% of China’s economy 
• $41bn rescue plan was launched in May…”a drop in the ocean” according to Moody’s analytics. 
• Goldman Sachs estimates $4.2 trillion unsold housing stock (x10 sales in 2023) 

Evergrande ordered to liquidate Evergrande defaults

Page 8

• China shifts growth due to collapse in property sector and inadequate domestic consumption 
• Focusing on batteries, solar panels, Electric Vehicles… 
• …but all industrial projects are approved to support investment and GDP – pulp & paper included 
• EU follows USA putting tariffs on Chinese EVs (and décor paper!) 

##### To what extent are China’s problems fixable?

Page 10

• Andy Rothman believes this is unsustainable and Xi Jinping will be obliged to change course, or risk social instability 
• Household savings could provide a major boost… 
• But for now, the focus is on self-sufficiency and industrial modernization 

##### China: Investment in P&B capacity far exceeds demand growth

Page 11

• China adding 20Mt of paper capacity in

2023 and 2024

• Xi Jinping mantra to “establish the new before abolishing the old”. 
• There are no old paper assets in China anymore !

#### Chinese exports of P&B

• Most exports go to other Asia, but Europe and USA are also important markets 
• Exports to Europe increased by 240,000t or 32% over the first 7 months, despite the Red Sea shipping crisis and rising freight rates 
• How will Chinese companies comply with EUDR? 
• Largest individual export markets are USA, Vietnam, India, Australia, Russia, Malaysia, Japan, UAE
